A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across the expanded evaluation and reorganized presentation.

before.justification: v1 reports original planning and formalization experiments on BlocksWorld-111 and MysteryBlocksWorld-100, including success counts and manually annotated error analyses in Tables 1–6.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments on BlocksWorld, MysteryBlocksWorld, Logistics, and Barman, with numerical results in Appendix C and manual error analyses in Tables 1–2.

M1.justification: Both versions generate complete PDDL domain and problem files from textual descriptions, use the same deterministic planner, and validate plans with VAL. Section 3 and the existing Appendix B prompts retain the same procedure; additional evaluated models do not establish a method change.

E1.justification: v2 adds package transportation in Logistics and cocktail preparation in Barman beyond the retained block-stacking domains. Appendix C reports Logistics evaluations at three naturalness levels and Barman evaluations with heavily templated descriptions, substantially broadening the task requirements tested.

E2.justification: v2 adds o3-mini to the formalizer-versus-planner comparisons on the retained BlocksWorld and MysteryBlocksWorld benchmarks. GPT-3.5-turbo and o1-preview results remain in the appendix despite their omission from the revised main model list. The baseline methodology remains direct planning.

E3.justification: BlocksWorld evaluation changes from 111 to 100 instances. Its stated stack-count range changes from 1 through the number of blocks to 2–15, without explaining whether instances were regenerated. v2 also adds model configurations, including limited Llama-405B and DeepSeek screening, and specifies Barman generation parameters. Zero-shot prompting, the planner, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 extends the existing naturalness analysis and manual analysis of 20 failed examples to Logistics, including detailed domain-file error categories. GPT-3.5-turbo rows disappear from the BlocksWorld and MysteryBlocksWorld error breakdowns. The lexical-perturbation analysis and sample Llama output case study are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report success counts and manually sampled error counts without repeated-run counts, random-seed specifications, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The expanded tables retain the same uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds Logistics, Barman, and o3-mini results and replaces BlocksWorld entries for the smaller evaluation set: GPT-4o natural-description correctness changes from 66/111 to 60/100, not a same-setting performance comparison. New results include o3-mini scoring 68/100 as formalizer versus 87/100 as planner on natural BlocksWorld, and every Barman formalizer scoring 0/100. Retained MysteryBlocksWorld model scores are unchanged.

T1.justification: Neither version develops theorems, proofs, or mathematical derivations. The planning concepts remain equivalent; shortened explanations and additional benchmark PDDL listings do not introduce a theoretical contribution.

C1.justification: The abstract and central contributions remain unchanged. The introduction and conclusion broaden claims from BlocksWorld and larger GPT models to several planning domains and Llama models up to 405B. The contribution summary now distinguishes open-model syntax errors from shared semantic errors, and the conclusion softens domains being absent from pretraining to being underrepresented.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 now acknowledges o3-mini's exception to the formalizer advantage, while Section 5.1 explicitly recognizes Gemma's strong MysteryBlocksWorld performance and discusses low-resource PDDL generation. New Appendix F discusses speed versus interpretability. The BlocksWorld-only limitation is removed, while zero-shot and simulated-domain limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A substantially expands dataset documentation with Logistics and Barman PDDL and description examples, IPC source years, the Barman generator and its 1–9 parameter ranges, and newly disclosed uniform complexity sampling for BlocksWorld. Existing hardware, KANI usage, prompts, repository access information, and licensing are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references concerning the wug test, code-generation benchmarking, DeepSeek-R1, PDDL generators, and IPC 2000. The central positioning against partial-PDDL approaches and the related-work comparison in Table 7 remain unchanged. PIC-to-IPC correction for the existing 1998 reference is bibliographic.

P1.justification: The main section order, abstract, and much of the introduction, methodology, and related work remain intact. Dataset and results paragraphs are revised, appendix results are consolidated into C.1–C.4, and an acknowledgment and brief methodology-comparison discussion are added.

P2.justification: The results presentation is substantially reorganized. Natural and templated BlocksWorld tables are combined in appendix Table 3; earlier error tables are merged and expanded. The original performance chart is reworked into separate domain and naturalness views, with new Logistics/Barman tables and a Barman figure. Figures 1–2 are retained with sizing or caption refinements.

improvement.justification: The Logistics and Barman experiments address v1's stated reliance on block-stacking, while o3-mini comparisons and expanded dataset documentation make the method's limits more informative. Reporting inconsistencies constrain these gains: v2 Figure 3 plots Gemma-2-27B near 10 on heavily templated BlocksWorld, whereas Table 3 reports 80/100, and broad headline claims are not fully reconciled with the new exceptions.
